newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy replaces scandal-stained railway chief.
newsitem.headline: Italy replaces scandal-stained railway chief.

text.p: The Italian government said on Friday it had appointed a replacement for Lorenzo Necci who resigned as managing director of the state railway after being arrested on suspicion of corruption.

The Treasury Ministry said in a statement that Giancarlo Cimoli, managing director of electricity company Edison, a division of the Montedison agri-industrial giant, would take over the helm at state railway Ferrovie dello Stato.
Cimoli, 57, has a degree in chemical engineering and three decades of experience in Italian public and private industry.
Among his chief tasks at the railway will be to oversee a multi-billion dollar project to build a new high-speed rail system across Italy.

The plan had been championed by Necci, who resigned on Thursday in a letter written from the prison cell in the northwest town of La Spezia where he is being held on suspicion of committing a raft of corruption-related offences.
Necci, 55, was arrested on September 15 on the orders of La Spezia magistrates investigating an alleged corrupt "super lobby" in state industries and the judiciary.
The Necci affair has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates probe allegations of trial-fixing and widespread bribes for state contracts.
Newspapers have dubbed the case "Tangentopoli 2", an echo of the "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) corruption scandal which exploded in 1992 and buried Italy's governing elite.
